finding.claim: Certificate publickey auth accepts any certificate signed by its own embedded CA key. The library never checks CA trust, cert_type, principals, or critical options, so an application handler that only checks the signature can be logged into by an attacker who self-signs a certificate.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied certificate bytes in the publickey USERAUTH_REQUEST (encrypted.rs:688-689).
finding.sink: handler.auth_openssh_certificate(user, cert) at encrypted.rs:782, which grants login when it returns Accept.

trace.note: Reads pubkey algorithm and key blob from the request.
Decodes the blob as a Certificate for cert algorithms.
cert.verify_signature() only checks the certificate against the CA key embedded in itself, not a trusted CA.
Takes the certificate's public key as the auth key.
Verifies the request signature with that key; the attacker holds the matching private key.
Passes the certificate to the application handler, which decides acceptance.
Default auth_openssh_certificate rejects, so exposure depends on the application overriding it.

finding.guards_checked: Expiry check (encrypted.rs:702-711); self-signature check (encrypted.rs:714); request signature over session id and packet (encrypted.rs:766-775); default handler rejects (server/mod.rs:291-297). Not present in library: CA trust check, cert_type == User check, principal-vs-username check, critical options (force-command, source-address). Verdict: PLAUSIBLE, depends on application handler.

finding.claim: Inbound channel-window flow control is not enforced. Data beyond the advertised window is delivered to the application, and the server keeps refilling the window, so an authenticated peer can send unbounded data.
finding.source: Size of CHANNEL_DATA / CHANNEL_EXTENDED_DATA sent by an authenticated peer, independent of its window.
finding.sink: chan.send(ChannelMsg::Data / ExtendedData) at server/encrypted.rs:1043-1046, delivering data to the application.

trace.note: Decrements sender_window_size only if data.len() <= sender_window_size; the comment says 'Ignore extra data' but the data is not dropped.
If the window is below target/2, queues a WINDOW_ADJUST to refill it, so the peer's over-window sends are never throttled.
Forwards the data to the channel regardless of window state.

finding.guards_checked: Per-packet size cap MAXIMUM_PACKET_LEN (cipher/mod.rs:313); per-channel mpsc buffer applies backpressure via send().await. No check that incoming data fits the advertised window. Requires authentication. Severity: low to medium (resource exhaustion and flow-control bypass).

finding.claim: No cap on the number of concurrently open channels. Each CHANNEL_OPEN allocates a Channel with an mpsc buffer of channel_buffer_size and stores it, so an authenticated peer can exhaust memory by opening channels without limit.
finding.source: Number of CHANNEL_OPEN messages sent by an authenticated peer.
finding.sink: Channel::new allocation at server/encrypted.rs:1574-1580 and insertion into per-session channel state.

trace.note: Allocates a new sender channel id; no count check.
Creates a Channel with channel_buffer_size (default 100, server/mod.rs:117) before the handler is consulted.

finding.guards_checked: Requires prior authentication. Grep of server code found no channels.len() or max-channel check. Not verified whether channels are removed when the handler rejects the open; if they are not, impact is larger. Severity: low; unverified on that point.
